newsitem.title: USA: U.S. disappointed that Belarus holds referendum.
newsitem.headline: U.S. disappointed that Belarus holds referendum.

text.p: The United States expressed disappointment on Monday at a decision by Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko to go ahead with a controversial referendum and called his victory "deprived of legitimacy."
More than 70 percent of the electorate in the former Soviet republic backed Lukashenko's referendum on a draft constitution on Sunday, giving him sweeping powers.

"We're quite disappointed that in Belarus yesterday the government went ahead with this referendum that has been labeled by the (Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe) and other international organisations as deprived of legitimacy," said State Department spokesman Glyn Davies.

Davies said there had been no open debate on the referendum, and other "serious electoral irregularities" had occurred, including the fact that the text of the referendum had not been made available to most voters.
"We don't view the process in Belarus as either free or fair in this referendum. It systemically deprived the opposition an opportunity to present its views," he said.

Davies said the government of Belarus could still declare the results of the referendum to be nonbinding, leaving the door open for compromise with parliament, which has vehemently opposed Lukashenko.

"We call on all parties to abide by OSCE principles and to pursue a course that avoids violence, coercion, and confrontation," Davies said. "President Lukashenko should seek compromise here, not confrontation."
